title: Some iPhone Duo screens aren’t making it through day one
summary: Unlucky early buyers say their iPhone Duo screens are cracking after just a few unfolds.
body: TL;DR Some early iPhone Duo owners are reporting cracked inner screens, with damage appearing near the crease. One owner says their screen broke after fewer than 20 unfolds, and Apple replaced the phone immediately. The cause and scale remain unclear, and it’s too early to establish whether there’s a broader design flaw. It’s October 23, and arguably the most-hyped smartphone of the year is finally starting to reach customers. Apple’s iPhone Duo is available starting today, and although supply is thin and delivery estimates unsightly , there’s a bigger reason that mars what should be a celebratory launch day. Early iPhone Duo buyers are facing problems with the new foldable’s hinge, with some reporting that the phone’s inner screens cracked after a handful of folds and unfolds. That’s not what you want to see, especially if you’re dropping $2,000 on a device.

title: Not a fan of full-screen Calling Cards? Keep an eye out for this update
summary: Google's working on a 'compact' option for Calling Card images.
body: TL;DR Google is working on a new Compact Photo option for Calling Cards in its Phone app. The option could let users display smaller contact photos instead of full-screen images. Four color presets have surfaced, potentially allowing users to customize the background behind these smaller photos. The feature isn’t functional yet. One of the Google Phone app ‘s coolest additions may have started out as a bit of a copy of Apple’s Contact Posters , but an upcoming option could help Google differentiate its implementation. The feature I’m talking about is Calling Cards , and it looks like Google wants to give users more flexibility over how they appear on your phone’s screen. Up until now, Calling Cards have appeared as full-screen images whenever a contact you’ve assigned an image to calls you — same as how Apple’s version works. But not everyone wants a huge image filling their phone’s entire screen every time someone calls. That’s what Google appears to be addressing.

summary: This leak may also give us some answers on the global release.
body: Credit: Samsung TL;DR The Galaxy Buds On were recently spotted listed on several European retail pages. The leak reveals that Samsung’s new earbuds could launch in Europe during the first half of December. Newly surfaced animations also provide a 360-degree look at the hardware. Samsung is getting ready to expand its audio device lineup with the addition of clip-on earbuds. Known as the Galaxy Buds On, the company finally confirmed the existence of the hardware earlier this month. The earbuds are scheduled to launch in South Korea on October 27. It’s still a mystery when they’ll be released in the US, but some retail pages may have given us a hint. A separate leak also provides our best look yet at the Galaxy Buds On. It’s possible that a release in the US could happen around the same time.

title: Tired of rebuilding patched APKs? These Morphe community projects handle them for you
summary: You can simplify patched Android app updates with self-hosted AutoMorph or cloud-based Mophe-AutoBuilds.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority TL;DR Manually updating Morphe-patched Android apps requires regularly and repeatedly downloading base APKs, running Morphe Manager, and applying updates by hand, potentially across multiple devices. AutoMorph automates the entire workflow via a Docker container on a homelab server. It automatically scrapes APKs, compiles builds daily, and supports custom keystores for seamless updates. Mophe-AutoBuilds pairs GitHub Actions with Obtainium for hands-off background updates, though it requires trusting pre-compiled APKs signed with shared community keys. Community patching tools, namely Morphe , have made it remarkably easy to tweak and de-bloat popular Android apps . However, keeping those patched apps up to date remains a persistent and manual chore. Users still have to routinely download APKs, fire up the Morphe Manager, apply routinely updated patch sets, and install the newly patched apps by hand. The process is tedious enough for one app; now imagine doing this for a handful of apps every time they get updated. A new open-source project dubbed AutoMorph aims to eliminate that friction entirely by moving the entire workflow to your self-…

Rather than letting the forgotten Alexa device gather more dust, they gave it an unexpected second career.

title: Some Android phones and Google Calendar events could soon be an hour off
summary: Android users in parts of Canada should check their phones before November 1.
body: TL;DR Parts of Canada are switching to permanent daylight saving time on November 1, ending seasonal clock changes. Google warns that Android phones running outdated software could incorrectly turn their clocks back by an hour. Some Google Calendar events could also shift by an hour, with certain appointments requiring manual corrections through the web version. The biannual tradition of changing clocks is coming to an end for a subset of the Canadian population, though with that convenience comes an added side of initial headaches. Permanent daylight saving time for British Columbia, Alberta, Manitoba, and the Northwest Territories starts on November 1, and with the date just a little over a week away at this point, Google wants to help Android users in those regions — or anyone traveling through them — make the transition. If the new rule hadn’t gone into effect, clocks in those regions would automatically turn back by an hour. Starting November 1, however, that won’t happen. While that sounds like a seamless transition, there’s a big catch here, especially for users who haven’t updated their Android devices.

title: Google Meet expands real-time translation across 63 languages
summary: The feature detects and translates 63 languages.
body: TL;DR Google Meet just added Gemini-powered speech translation across 63 languages. The feature automatically detects spoken languages and translates them in audio and captions for individual participants. Real-time translation starts rolling out to some eligible users today. Meetings are meant to facilitate communication, but anyone who’s been in one that could have been an email, as the saying goes, knows that’s not always the case. That’s even more true for teams with multilingual members. Now Google Meet has a solution with Gemini-powered speech translation for 63 languages on web and mobile devices. In a new Workspace blog entry , Google shares that Meet users will be able to turn on speech translation for themselves in their preferred language at any point in a meeting using a dedicated translation control in the meeting toolbar. Google Meet will then automatically detect what language is being spoken and translate it for the user, both audibly and in captions. Google claims this translation takes place in “near real-time.”

title: Pour one out for Arc: One of the most hyped browsers is shutting down for good
summary: And we now know exactly when.
body: TL;DR The Browser Company has confirmed that Arc browser will shut down on December 22, 2026. New account registrations have already stopped, while Arc Search will lose its AI features and account syncing on November 23. Arc will stop working on Windows and macOS on December 22, and users can export their data before the shutdown. The writing has been on the wall for a while now, and it’s just been confirmed that one of the most hyped-up browsers is being shut down. The browser I’m talking about is Arc , and its days are numbered. We reported last year that The Browser Company had stopped active development on Arc to focus on an AI-first browser called Dia . Since then, Arc has been in maintenance mode, receiving only security updates and bug fixes. Now, the company is ready to take Arc off life support altogether, and we have a clear timeline of what’s happening next.

title: Google sounds like it’s had enough of the US renaming bodies of water
summary: After the Gulf of America and Lake America, Google resists rebranding the Atlantic.
body: TL;DR Over the past couple years, the US has been rejecting the established names of various bodies of water, renaming them after itself. Popular mapping apps like Google Maps have so far largely adopted those new names. Now Google CEO Sundar Pichai has reportedly drawn the line at efforts to rename the Atlantic Ocean. Things are weird right now in America. The current administration has expressed little interest in abiding by traditional norms, and that’s arguably no clearer than in its unprecedented efforts to rename international bodies of water with jingoistic “American” titles. While Google Maps has so far demonstrated nothing but willingness to deface its maps with the new names, it turns out that there may be one line it’s just not interested in crossing. Yesterday evening, reports The Washington Post , the president told a crowd in South Carolina that he asked Google CEO Sundar Pichai whether he’d be up to “handle” renaming the Atlantic Ocean.

title: Some T-Mobile customers may finally get something back for those unexpected price hikes (Updated)

body: TL;DR T-Mobile has reached a settlement in New York over its controversial 2024 price hikes, potentially delivering more than $38 million in benefits to affected customers. Eligible customers can receive refunds, free 5G phones, or upgrade credits, while those who stay will have their plan prices frozen until at least 2029. The settlement only applies to affected New Yorkers, with no similar relief announced for customers in other states. Update, October 22, 2026 (4:46 PM ET): T-Mobile has responded to Android Authority ‘s inquiry with the following statement: The $38 million cited in the press release is an estimate of potential benefits that a group of long-standing T-Mobile customers may choose to take advantage of, not the amount in refunds or payments. The agreement provides for approximately $98,000 paid to the state and a range of optional customer benefits. We’re glad to have this matter resolved and remain focused on delivering value to our customers.

title: Google Sheets is finally catching up to Excel with support for more chart types
summary: Box and whisker charts are finally here in Google Sheets.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Google Sheets is rolling out support for box and whisker charts. If you select a range of numeric values, Sheets will calculate the minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile, maximum, mean, and outliers automatically without helper formulas. Box and whisker charts imported from Excel are now preserved, with data references, calculations, and formatting intact. Box and whisker charts are useful for displaying the distribution of data within a population. While they have long been a staple for Microsoft Excel, that hasn’t been the case for Google Sheets. However, Google is fixing that problem with a new update. Google Sheets is finally gaining native support for box and whisker charts. When you want to create one, you’ll just have to select a range of raw numeric values. Google says Sheets will automatically calculate the minimum, first quartile, median, third quartile, maximum, mean, and outliers for you. And best of all, you won’t need to use any helper formulas to accomplish this.

title: Put down your pitchforks — Google’s not hiding YouTube’s dislike button
summary: At least, not where it matters.
body: TL;DR YouTube users recently started reporting that they were finding their dislike button hidden away. Google now confirms that this change only appears for your own uploaded videos. Is there any relationship between a streaming service and its users that’s more contentious than YouTube’s? Even putting the interminable struggle between YouTube and ad blockers aside for the moment, it feels like nearly every single change the service makes to its interface is met with fierce pushback . Earlier this week, we told you about the newest controversy, as some viewers reported that the dislike button in videos was being hidden away , out of reach. As it turns out, this latest one might be no big deal, after all. As we shared at the time, impacted users observed that rather than finding the dislike button out in the open, perched right next to its like-button brother, YouTube was moving the the option behind a three-dot overflow menu — putting you one more tap removed from being able to dislike a video. It wasn’t the end of the world, but it did admittedly feel like YouTube was going out of its way to discourage negative feedback.

title: Android handhelds are running PS5 games now
summary: Not big 3D PS5 games, but PS5 games nonetheless.
body: TL;DR An Android PlayStation 5 emulator called CapyPS5 is currently able to run a handful of PS5 games at playable frame rates. The games were tested on the AYN Odin 3, a relatively powerful Android-based game handheld. The emulator is currently in alpha. Emulation’s nothing new on Android — with a little elbow grease, it’s fairly easy to get Xbox, PlayStation, and Switch games running on your phone or game handheld. Now, somebody’s even got PS5 games up and running on the AYN Odin 3 . Ghael, developer of the Lemon Switch emulator we covered last week, is back at it with CapyPS5 . Based on the FEX x86-64 emulator and KytyPS5 PlayStation 5 translation layer for desktop operating systems, CapyPS5 is a work in progress, but Ghael’s already got a handful of PS5 games running well on Android.

title: Thanks, Apple: Variable aperture and curved displays could be coming back to Android
summary: Chinese Android OEMs are reportedly considering these hardware upgrades for future flagships.
body: TL;DR A reliable source of leaks claims Chinese smartphone brands are considering variable aperture camera setups with a 200MP camera, following the iPhone 18 Pro’s release. Companies are also reportedly considering borderless quad-curved screens, possibly in anticipation of next year’s rumored 20th-anniversary iPhone. Smartphone brands like Samsung and others have previously launched phones with dual-aperture camera systems. The Apple iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max introduced a 48MP primary camera with a variable aperture , a first for the iPhone lineup. We’re now learning that Android smartphone brands, particularly in China, may take cues from this hardware addition for their upcoming devices. According to a machine-translated post from leaker Digital Chat Station on Weibo , “several” Chinese phone makers are considering a variable aperture lens for future devices. Interestingly, these brands seem to be considering pairing this mechanism with a massive 200MP sensor.

title: Durability tests reveal how the iPhone Duo handles thousands of continuous folds
summary: Apple's titanium hinge holds up, but the inner display crease has its own story to tell.
body: Credit: Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority TL;DR Automated stress tests by YouTuber Tim Pan (10,500 folds plus sub-zero testing) and Joanna Stern (over 32,000 folds) show that the iPhone Duo’s 3D-printed titanium hinge remains sturdy and smooth all throughout. However, continuous folding significantly deepens the inner display crease, both visually and to the touch. Other iPhone Duo quirks include single-sided NFC positioning, lack of an internal earpiece (forcing speakerphone when open), minor thermal throttling, and UI misfires when opened slowly. Apple spent years watching Android OEMs pioneer the foldable landscape, and then made deliberate design choices to ensure its first folding iPhone wouldn’t suffer from the same teething issues as early Galaxy Fold generations. Much of that engineering effort centers on the iPhone Duo’s inner display , which uses a custom nano-texture finish to diffuse reflections and minimize the visible groove down the center. However, physics remains undefeated: a new extreme durability test shows that after 10,000 folds, that subtle crease deepens considerably. title: These 2 useful Google Wallet upgrades are starting to roll out
summary: Google Wallet's latest additions are beginning to appear, but not for everyone.
body: TL;DR Google Wallet’s new in-app notification feed is beginning to reach users. Passport-based ID passes are also expanding to more countries. Both additions are rolling out gradually, so not everyone may have them yet. Google Wallet has become a handy home for everything from payment cards to boarding passes, but keeping track of changes to those saved items hasn’t always been straightforward. Google is now addressing that inconvenience with a dedicated notification feed and expanding its digital passport feature to more countries. The notification feed isn’t entirely unexpected. Earlier this month, we reported that Google’s October Play Services update promised an in-app message center for Wallet, but didn’t explain where users would find it. Now, 9to5Google reports that the feature is starting to appear within the app.

title: I’ve never owned smart glasses, but Samsung’s Android XR glasses may change that
summary: Android XR might have what it takes.
body: Credit: Jonathan Feist / Android Authority I will admit that I got pretty swept up by the VR and AR craze, especially in the early days. From the HTC Vive to later mixed-reality devices like the Meta Quest 3, I’ve had my share of these devices. I’ve even spent time with earlier headsets and wearable displays, but I’ve never once felt the need to invest in a pair of smart glasses. That might finally change, as Samsung’s long-anticipated Android XR glasses are reportedly on the way this November. Samsung’s glasses come at a time when there are already a growing number of competitors on Meta’s platform, but none have piqued my interest enough to consider a purchase. Meta-based glasses have a fair share of capabilities, including taking photos and videos, sharing to the cloud, music playback, live translation, and even asking questions or identifying objects using Meta.

title: Google’s refurbished Pixel 9 might be the smartest phone purchase of 2026
summary: The best way to beat rising smartphone prices.
body: The state of the smartphone market in 2026 is quietly getting quite worrying. Sure, we have Apple finally jumping onto the foldable phone bandwagon with the iPhone Duo , and brands like OPPO and vivo continue to deliver some excellent camera smartphones . But there’s no denying that rising memory prices, and consequently higher smartphone prices, are starting to affect the market. Samsung recently increased the prices of its Galaxy S26 series , which means even the base Galaxy S26 now starts at a whopping $1,000 in the US. And the impact is starting to show in sales figures as well, with the smartphone market reportedly seeing a 20% decline in sales , the biggest drop in nearly 14 years.
